title: Witness and Inheritance
premise: Dominic Nystrom, the reclusive archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, receives two letters in the same hand: one confessing to a drowning thirty years ago, the other promising a second confession if she can find the writer before the spring tide. Following the letters through the cathedral's sealed crypt and a tangle of alibis built by four childhood friends, Dominic discovers the drowned boy was her own mother's brother—and that her mentor, Canon Ellery Voss, helped bury the truth that made her an orphan raised by strangers. In the climax, the tide exposes the crypt's flooded lower vault, where the final letter waits; the confessor is Voss himself, dying and unable to speak it aloud. Dominic must choose between exposing him and claiming the found family of witnesses—parishioners, police, and the victim's surviving sister—who help her close the case on her own terms.
about_author: Ulyana Fairweather is a former parish records volunteer who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters in coastal church archives. She writes mysteries about people who hide inside institutions, and about the documents that refuse to let them.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Dominic Nystrom's POV. While cataloguing bequests, she finds two letters addressed to 'The Archivist'—one confessing to a killing at Graywater Point thirty years ago, one promising more if she can identify its author. The emotional beat: her careful invisibility cracks as curiosity overrides caution.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She petitions Canon Ellery Voss for access to the crypt her predecessor sealed; he refuses too quickly, citing flood damage. She notices his hands shake at the name Graywater. Beat: first suspicion that the institution itself is complicit.

chapters.title: Alibi of the Tide Table
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with a flashback fragment. The 1994 tide tables show the drowning was impossible when the confessing letter claims—someone is lying about time itself. Beat: the pleasure of a puzzle, shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Sister of the Drowned
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Maren Oduya, who lost her twin brother Casper at Graywater Point. She remembers four friends swearing silence and one who never stopped writing unsent letters. Beat: grief reopened after thirty years of enforced forgetting.

chapters.title: Four Names in the Register
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The baptismal register yields four names: Voss, a now-dead fisherman, a vanished schoolteacher, and Maren herself. Each had an airtight alibi—too airtight, all corroborated by the same witness. Beat: the pattern tightens.

chapters.title: What the Confession Gets Wrong
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Forensic reading shows the confession contains errors only an innocent person—or someone protecting another—would make. Beat: doubt curdles into obsession; Dominic realizes she's being led.

chapters.title: The Vanished Schoolteacher
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She tracks Iris Penhale, the fourth friend, living under a changed name inland. Iris admits they lied—but not about who killed Casper. About who else was there. Beat: terror of a memory surfacing.

chapters.title: A Second Letter Arrives
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A third letter appears inside a returned donation envelope: a page of Casper's own handwriting, dated after his death. Someone has been forging a dead boy's hand for decades. Beat: vertigo—the case is older and stranger than murder.

chapters.title: Orphan Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, intimate. Digging into Casper's file, she finds her own adoption papers adjacent to his death record—her mother was the unnamed fifth friend no one mentions. Beat: the investigation turns inward; identity destabilizes.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Corroborated Everyone
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Every alibi traces back to young Ellery Voss, then a curate, who 'saw' each friend elsewhere. Maren confronts him; he neither denies nor confirms. Beat: betrayal—the man who raised half the town's trust may have built the lie.

chapters.title: Flood Damage
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. An engineer's report reveals the crypt's lower vault flooded in 1994—the same week Casper died—and was sealed by order of the dean, Voss's mentor. Beat: the architecture itself is an accomplice.

chapters.title: Iris Breaks
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Pressed by Maren, Iris recalls the night: Casper alive, arguing with someone in clerical grey, the five children fleeing as the tide came in. They agreed to identical stories to protect—she still can't say whom. Beat: guilt as a shared inheritance.

chapters.title: The Handwriting Match
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Comparing the forged pages with cathedral sermons, she matches the forger's hand to Voss across thirty years—he has been writing as Casper, keeping the boy 'alive' on paper. Beat: horror braided with pity.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Archive
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She lays the evidence before Voss. He admits only this: 'I wrote what should have survived.' He gives her the crypt key and three days until the spring tide. Beat: the mentor becomes the mystery; mercy wars with duty.

chapters.title: Maren's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She tells Dominic about the fifth friend—Liesl, Dominic's mother—who saw everything and fled, giving up her child rather than raise her inside the lie. Beat: Dominic learns she was protected, not abandoned.

chapters.title: What Liesl Saw
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, interleaved with her mother's recovered journal. Liesl's account: the dean, not Voss, struck Casper during an argument over stolen church funds; Voss helped cover it to save the cathedral and the children from scandal. Beat: moral ground shifting beneath every certainty.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Archivist
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Police want the full truth; the parish wants peace; Voss is dying. Dominic realizes closing the case means deciding what the record will say—an archivist's power she never wanted. Beat: the weight of testimony.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. At low tide, the sea withdraws enough to open the lower vault. Inside: Casper's actual effects, the dean's embezzlement ledger, and Voss's final letter, written in his own hand at last. Beat: the past physically surfaces.

chapters.title: The Final Letter
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Voss's letter confesses everything: the cover-up, the forgeries, his decades of guardianship-by-guilt—and names Dominic as the heir to both the archive and the truth. He dies that night. Beat: grief for a flawed father figure.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She gives the ledger and letter to the police but testifies to the whole chain—dean, cover-up, coerced children—refusing the tidy version. The dead dean's family retaliates; the parish wavers. Beat: cost of honesty, paid willingly.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren, Iris, and Dominic scatter Casper's recovered effects at Graywater Point. Maren claims Dominic as niece-in-spirit; Iris forgives herself aloud. Beat: warmth earned through shared truth rather than blood.

chapters.title: The Open Crypt
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, coda. She unseals the crypt permanently as a public archive, files the true record, and keeps one blank envelope in her drawer—for whoever confesses next. Beat: quiet resolution; identity chosen, inheritance accepted, vigilance kept.
